result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.trav_out_edge()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Traverse from selected nodes to outbound edges. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L17008-L17051){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.trav_out_edge() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Traverse to outbound edges](/assets/graphs/trav-out-edge.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Left: in a seven-node directed graph, node C is selected (accent). Right: after trav_out_edge() the node selection is gone and the two edges leaving C, C to B and C to D, are selected instead (accent)." width="100%"} From the currently selected nodes, moves to all edges where the selected nodes are sources (outbound edges). The current node selection is cleared and replaced with an edge selection. For directed graphs, selects edges where from=selected_node. For undirected graphs, selects all edges incident to selected nodes. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Traversing from "A" to its outbound edges replaces the node selection with an edge selection -- here, both edges leaving "A": ::: {#5214716c .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph(directed=True) graph.add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) graph.add_edges([("A", "B"), ("A", "C")]) node_a_id = graph.get_id_from_label("A") graph.select_nodes_by_id([node_a_id]).trav_out_edge() len(graph.get_selected_edge_ids()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 2 ``` ::: :::
